en: The Analysis of the Bhikkhunī Rules,
For a lustful bhikkhunī who consents to physical contact with a lustful man, how many of the six origins of offenses do those offenses originate from?
For a lustful bhikkhunī who consents to physical contact with a lustful man, those offenses originate from one of the six origins of offenses—namely, from the origin [of offense] by way of volition.
They originate from both body and mind, not from speech …pe….
For one who requests curd and then eats it, how many of the six origins of offenses do those offenses originate from?
For one who requests curd and then eats it, those offenses originate from four of the six origins of offenses.
There may be [an offense] that originates from the body, but not from speech or mind;
there may be one that originates from both body and speech, but not from the mind;
there may be one that originates from both body and mind, but not from speech.
They may arise from body, speech, and mind.
The fifth section on origination is finished.
